definitionOfDone: `design.read` is in MCP_SERVED_QUERY_KINDS (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:27) AND in QUERY_HANDLERS (mcp-dispatch-port.ts:297). An agent-authenticated `design.read` over the MCP port RETURNS the design-store answer (latest revision, or DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT with code AND layer). A query advertised without a handler is an unserved capability.

An agent-authenticated `design.submit` over the MCP port REACHES the handler (the kind is a command, so it is served by NOT being in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS). Assert it is absent from that exclusion roster and from HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. Copying the human-only pattern here would make the design step unstaffable.

taskRails: A SERVED QUERY NEEDS BOTH a roster entry and a dispatch handler. One without the other is an advertised capability the port cannot serve.
Call readDesignRevision. Do not reimplement the aggregate. No vocabulary, registry, or generated-client edits — those are task-06ac0da1.
SEAT KINDS, NOT HUMAN GATES. Do not add design.submit or design.read to MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS or HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS.

implementationPlan.description: READ THE TWO CONTRACTS BEFORE WRITING AGAINST THEM. Record in the step note the exact shape of `DesignReadInput` and `DesignReadResult` from apps/daemon/src/design/design-store.ts (readDesignRevision is at :189, taking `store: SqliteEventStore`), and the full refusal roster in design/design-contracts.ts (DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT maps to layer "LEDGER" at :71 - name every other code that read path can return, because global rail 1 requires the arm to assert the SPECIFIC code and its layer, and a second refusal layer answering first is how these tests go vacuous). Also record how config.deps exposes a store to a query handler, by reading answerWorkContextQuery in mcp-work-context-query.ts and answerProductContractRead at mcp-dispatch-port.ts:277 - the port config injects narrow ports (contract, documents, graph, affordances), so design.read needs the same treatment rather than reaching for a store directly.
implementationPlan.note:
CONTRACTS READ. One finding materially corrects DoD 4's payload sentence.

DesignReadInput (design-store.ts:58) is `{ goalRef: string; projectId: string; version?: number }` — THREE members. `projectId` is REQUIRED, and DoD 4 says the payload is "`{goalRef}` plus optional `version`, matching DesignReadInput". Those cannot both be literally true. They are reconciled the way graph.get already resolves the same problem, and the reconciliation is a SECURITY property, not a convenience: `projectId` comes from the AUTHENTICATED PRINCIPAL, never from the payload. `AuthenticatedPrincipal` carries `{capabilities, principalId, projectId}` at http/http-contract.ts:119-123, and planning/graph-query.ts:13-18 states the rule outright — "`principal.projectId` ... cross-checked against the port's `boundProjectId`. Both halves matter — the principal check stops a principal from a different project being served by this daemon at all." So a payload-supplied projectId would be a cross-project read primitive. The wire payload therefore stays exactly `{goalRef}` or `{goalRef, version}` as DoD 4 says, and a payload that CARRIES projectId is refused as an unknown key. DoD 4 is met in the sense that matters; the apparent mismatch is recorded here rather than silently resolved.

DesignReadResult (design-store.ts:69) is `{ok: true, record: DesignRecord, versions: readonly number[]} | DesignRefusal`. `readDesignRevision` (:189) reads events, decodes each, refuses DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED when a decoded record's projectId or goalRef does not match the input (so the principal-sourced projectId is genuinely enforced at the aggregate), refuses DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT on an empty aggregate AND on a `version` that no record carries, and otherwise returns the latest record plus every version ever appended.

REFUSAL ROSTER, complete, from design-contracts.ts:65-79 `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` (the code list is DERIVED from these keys, so the two cannot disagree). Codes the READ path can return, with layers: DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT -> LEDGER; DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED -> LEDGER; DESIGN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE -> LEDGER. The other three are submit-path only: DESIGN_CONTRACT_NOT_APPROVED -> CONTRACT_AUTHORITY, DESIGN_REVISION_CONFLICT -> LEDGER, DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID -> REQUEST. `DesignRefusal` (:106) is `{code, layer, ok: false, sourceCode, sourceLayer}` — the layer travels ON the refusal, so global rail 1's code-AND-layer assertion reads both off one value. Layers are the closed set CONTRACT_AUTHORITY | LEDGER | REQUEST (:57).

PORT INJECTION, confirmed against the two precedents. `QueryHandler` (mcp-dispatch-port.ts:149) is `(envelope, context, config) => Uint8Array`. Helpers: `bytesOf` (:91), `queryRefusal()` (:132) which emits `{error: createRuntimeError({code: "INPUT_INVALID"}), ok: false}`, `authenticatorOf(deps)` (:140). `ProductContractReadPort` (product-contract-read-port.ts:55) is the narrow-port shape to copy — a one-method interface `{read(goalRef: unknown): ProductContractReadResult}` built by a factory that CLOSES OVER `{projectId, store}` (:63-66), so the port never takes a raw store from the handler. design.read gets the same treatment: a `DesignReadPort` with one `read` method, created over the store, with the handler supplying the principal's projectId.

BRIDGE SHAPE confirmed: `apps/daemon/src/mcp-work-context-query.js` is exactly one line, `export * from "./mcp-work-context-query.ts";`. The new module's bridge mirrors it.

No files edited in this step.

implementationPlan.description: THE HANDLER, IN ITS OWN MODULE. Create apps/daemon/src/mcp-design-read-query.ts exporting `answerDesignReadQuery`, modelled on answerProductContractRead (mcp-dispatch-port.ts:277-294) and sited like answerWorkContextQuery (imported at :22) - NOT inline, because mcp-dispatch-port.ts is already 376 lines against a 400 split bar. Order of operations copied exactly: refuse when the injected port is absent; `authenticateHttpRequest(authenticatorOf(config.deps), context?.credential ?? config.fallbackCredential ?? null, WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION)` and return its refusal bytes when not ok; refuse a non-object/array/null payload; THEN the key check. The key check is NOT the sibling's `Object.keys(request).length !== 1` (risk R3): design.read takes `{goalRef}` plus OPTIONAL `version`, so admit exactly {goalRef} or {goalRef, version}, require goalRef to be a string, and refuse any unknown key. Delegate to the existing `readDesignRevision` - do not reimplement the aggregate (task rail 2). Create the sibling apps/daemon/src/mcp-design-read-query.js bridge in the same step; every mcp-*.ts in that directory has one and a missing bridge typechecks clean while failing at runtime. Keep the module under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
HANDLER LANDED, 111 lines, plus its one-line .js bridge. `npx tsc --project tsconfig.json --noEmit` from apps/daemon => EXIT 0 (first attempt was EXIT 1 on two unused imports, TS6196 HttpDispatchContext and TS6133 WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION; both removed, and their absence is correct — the protocol version arrives on the request object exactly as answerGraphQuery takes it, so the module has no business naming the constant itself).

SHAPE: `answerDesignReadQuery(request: DesignReadQueryRequest): Uint8Array`, taking `{authenticator, body, credential, port, protocolVersion}`. That is answerGraphQuery's request-object shape rather than answerProductContractRead's `(envelope, context, config)` — deliberately. The QueryHandler signature belongs to the dispatch table, so keeping this module free of McpDispatchPortConfig lets it be tested without constructing a port config, and step 5 supplies the thin adapter. `DesignReadPort` is the one-method `{read(input: DesignReadInput): DesignReadResult}`, closed over its store by the composer exactly as createProductContractReadPort does.

ORDER IS THE BEHAVIOUR, documented in the module: absent port refuses first, then authentication, then payload shape. Authentication precedes the shape check so an unidentified caller never learns whether a payload was well formed; the absent-port check precedes it because a daemon composed without design support has no answer either way.

projectId COMES OFF `access.principal.projectId`, NEVER THE PAYLOAD. This is the row's one real security decision and it is load-bearing: `readDesignRevision` (design-store.ts:196-201) matches the STORED record's projectId against the INPUT, so a caller-supplied projectId would simply agree with itself and yield a cross-project read primitive. A payload naming `projectId` is refused as an unknown key.

PAYLOAD DECODE, three deliberate choices beyond the plan text:
1. `DESIGN_READ_PAYLOAD_KEYS` is a whitelist loop, not `Object.keys(request).length !== 1` (risk R3 — copying the sibling verbatim would have refused every `{goalRef, version}`). Unknown keys REFUSE rather than being ignored: an ignored key lets a caller believe a filter applied that never did.
2. `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` for both values, for the reason graph-query.ts:145-157 gives about its own body — an inherited or ACCESSOR-bearing key must not answer for the caller, since a getter would run inside the daemon and could return a different value on its second read than the one validated.
3. `version` is gated by `Number.isSafeInteger(version) && version >= 0`, which rejects NaN, Infinity, 1.5 and 2**53 in one predicate. Not decoration: an unsafe version can never match a stored record, so admitting it would convert a malformed request into a DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT that reads to the agent like a real answer about the goal.

Delegates wholly to the existing `readDesignRevision` via the port. No aggregate logic reimplemented (task rail 2). Not yet wired into QUERY_HANDLERS — that is step 5 — so this commit adds a module nothing calls yet; the consumer edge lands two steps from now.

implementationPlan.description: HANDLER TESTS, refusal codes pinned (DoD 2, global rail 1). New apps/daemon/src/mcp-design-read-query.test.ts. Prove each refusal arm by mutating the production surface until it reds, and quote the red in the step note - a refusal test that has never been seen to fail is not evidence.

11 ARMS, ALL GREEN, EVERY REFUSAL DRILLED. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json --no-file-parallelism src/mcp-design-read-query.test.ts` => `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 11 passed (11)`, EXIT 0, 7.35s.

Driven by a REAL file-backed store through the production journey (boundWorld -> committedRevision -> approveGate1 -> submitDesignRevision), never a hand-built record, so a green read proves the aggregate was reached rather than a fixture echoed. closeStores() in afterAll for Windows handle discipline.

ONE FIXTURE NOTE worth carrying: http-test-fixtures.ts `authenticator()` mints `projectId: "proj-0001"`, and no design aggregate here is written under that id, so it CANNOT drive a green arm. Reaching one through it would have meant weakening the projectId check — i.e. testing the weakening. The test builds its own authenticator parameterised by projectId instead, which is also what makes the cross-project arm expressible.

MUTATION DRILLS (global rail 1). Backup out of tree at %TEMP%/mcp-design-read-query.worker-d6e44333.bak; the module is UNTRACKED (`??`), so `git diff` would certify nothing and restore is proved by SHA256 (global rail 13):

- D1 delete the unknown-key whitelist loop => `Tests 2 failed | 9 passed (11)`. Red: "refuses a payload that names projectId, rather than honouring it" and "refuses an unknown key, a missing goalRef, and a non-string goalRef". `AssertionError: expected true to be false`.
- D2 FIRST ATTEMPT WAS A WEAK MUTATION AND STAYED GREEN — recording it because the reason is the interesting part. I replaced the principal read with `payload.projectId ?? principal.projectId`; all 11 stayed green, because the whitelist REFUSES a payload carrying projectId before that line is ever reached. The two guards are coupled, so a payload-shaped mutation cannot reach the projectId source. That is a property of the design, not a hole in the suite, but it means the obvious drill proves nothing.
- D2b, the mutation that actually bites: hard-code `projectId: "project-1"` in place of `access.principal.projectId` => `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`, red on "refuses a principal bound to ANOTHER project". THIS is the arm that pins the security decision; the cross-project principal is answered from the wrong project's aggregate the moment the principal stops being the source.
- D3 drop `Number.isSafeInteger(version) && version >= 0`, keeping only the typeof check => `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`, red on "refuses a version that is not a safe non-negative integer".
- D4 replace `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(request, "goalRef")` with `request["goalRef"]` => `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`, red on "refuses a goalRef reachable only through the prototype or a getter".

RESTORE PROVED, in a call SEPARATE from the restore: `sha256sum` on the module and the backup both `80ce5240e6ae725e3ec40217d259f138f2e8944a636be61f6cb7b3fab2bc160b`. Re-run after restore: 11 passed (11), EXIT 0.

DoD 2 is met on the read half: the green arm asserts the revision by exact content (toStrictEqual against the fixture) plus goalRef, projectId, version and the versions list; DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT is asserted with CODE and LAYER "LEDGER" from an AUTHENTICATED caller, and the code-layer pairing is cross-checked against DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS so a future remap cannot leave the literal stale. The unauthenticated arm asserts stage AUTHENTICATE and that NO design code appears anywhere in the answer, which is what stops a handler that read first and refused later from passing.
